name: Ironveil Splitback Recon Rig
description: Built for runners whose work takes them across rooftops, through maintenance shafts, and back onto the street without a wardrobe change. The core garment is a deep burgundy-to-black ombre tactical hoodie with a full back panel split from collar to hem — a geneware accommodation for wing or spinal rig users, closed with quick-release mag-clips that hold flush and silent. The front is structured with four concealed cargo pockets behind a smooth face fabric that reads as a plain athletic pullover; the interior houses a flat holster sleeve on the left chest and a tool loop array across the right. The hood is reinforced with a wire frame that shapes it into a face-shadowing cowl without looking tactical. Below, the bottoms are a pair of deep plum ripstop cargo trousers with articulated knee panels, a concealed prosthetic channel along the outer left leg, and two ankle-level dump pockets accessible by touch. The waistband integrates a thin battery routing strip for chrome lower-body augmentation. Footwear is a matte graphite split-sole rooftop boot with a textured grip tread and magnetic toe-cap. A slim chest harness worn over the hoodie carries the only visible gear — a pair of utility pouches that read as a courier rig.
functionality: Full back panel split with mag-clips for wing or spinal rig accommodation, concealed chest holster and tool loops, prosthetic channel in left trouser leg, ankle dump pockets, battery routing waistband strip, face-shadowing reinforced hood, rooftop grip split-sole boot
what_it_says: The burgundy-to-black fade is a runner's signature color — not flashy enough to mark you as Spire, not drab enough to read as pure Shelf. The visible courier harness is deliberate misdirection. Anyone clocking the boot sole and the way the hood sits knows this person does vertical work. The split back is the tell for those who know geneware — it says this runner doesn't hide what they are.
worn_by: geneware-modified runners with wing or spinal rigs
runners with significant lower-body chrome who need routing accommodation
manufacturer: Scaleback Workshop — independent fabricator, no fixed address, takes commissions through dead drops
story_hooks: The mag-clips on the back panel are rated for a standard wing span — but a runner's geneware has been modified beyond spec, and mid-jump across a transit shaft the clips fail, the panel flares open, and suddenly they're very visible against a lit window.

A fence recognizes the Scaleback Workshop stitching on the interior collar and knows the fabricator only takes jobs for a specific network. This runner is either connected — or wearing a dead runner's rig.

The courier harness pouches are searched at a Tier 3 building entrance. They're clean. But the guard runs a secondary scan and the battery routing strip in the waistband registers as a restricted augmentation power draw — above civilian legal limits.
related_entities: NeuralPath LinkGuard Secure Civic Identity BCI

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, utilitarian silhouette that reads athletic from the front but reveals tactical sophistication on closer inspection. The ombre hoodie creates a graduated shadow effect from burgundy to near-black, while the split back panel hints at augmentation without announcing it. Worn by someone built for vertical movement and rapid transitions between environments. Layered visual complexity — smooth face fabric conceals serious functionality.
physical_description.fit: Tailored compression through the torso with strategic articulation at shoulders and hips. The hoodie sits close enough to not snag on rooftop edges but loose enough to accommodate internal holsters and padding. Cargo trousers are fitted at the thigh but cut with gussets at the knee for climbing and crouching. Overall impression: movement-optimized, not restrictive.
physical_description.primary_material: Ballistic weave blend for the hoodie (burgundy-black ombre treatment); ripstop nylon for cargo trousers in deep plum; matte-finish synthetic leather reinforcements at stress points. Battery routing strip is flexible polymer composite.
physical_description.texture: Smooth, almost liquid-feeling face fabric on the hoodie belies the armor underneath. Ripstop creates a subtle grid pattern visible in certain light angles. Back split panel has clean, flush magnetic closures with minimal surface drag. Hood interior is lined with soft friction-weave for silent, secure fitting.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep burgundy fading to near-black across the back and shoulders (ombre effect). Plum cargo bottoms create a monochromatic, low-visibility palette. Matte graphite boots ground the look. Mag-clip closures and battery strip are brushed steel — only glint when deliberately exposed.
physical_description.closures: Magnetic quick-release clips along the back split (silent, secure, fast separation for geneware access). Hoodie drawstring is woven steel-core. Cargo pockets use friction-fit magnetic flaps. Trousers fasten with a hidden side-zip and magnetic waistband integration.
distinctive_features: Removable back split panel with flush-mounted quick-release mag-clips (geneware accommodation)
Four concealed cargo pockets behind smooth face fabric
Flat holster sleeve integrated into left chest interior
Tool loop array across right interior (up to 6 loops)
Wire-framed hood shaped into a face-shadowing cowl
Articulated knee panels with concealed prosthetic channel on left outer leg
Ankle dump pockets accessible by touch alone
Battery routing strip woven into waistband (for chrome lower-body augmentation)
Slim chest harness with two utility pouches (reads as courier rig)
Split-sole rooftop boot with magnetic toe-cap
Textured grip tread across both sole sections
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 boundary. The build quality and customization suggest someone with serious Φ to spend or serious connections (Scaleback Workshop commissions aren't cheap). But the tactical functionality and wear-ready aesthetic prevent it from reading as Tier 1 luxury — this is built for work, not display.
physical_description.cultural_context: Runner kit. Someone who moves through the city vertically and horizontally, who needs to blend on the street but operate in the margins. Likely augmented (the back split and battery routing don't exist on baseline anatomy). Suggests self-sufficiency, operational discipline, and access to fabricators outside corporate supply chains. Not military (too individual, too custom), not corpo (too visibly tactical), but street-level operative — extraction runner, infiltration specialist, courier with secondary capabilities.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. The ombre fades slightly unevenly from actual use (rooftop weathering, body heat wear patterns). Mag-clips show minor shine from repeated open/close cycles. Holster sleeve interior has subtle creasing from regular loadout cycles. Cargo pocket seams show honest use but no tears — Scaleback builds last. Boots have scuff marks on the toe-cap from rooftop landings but the grip tread is still sharp.
